**Quinn Foster**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:**
HMSA Member Advocacy & Appeals
Appeals Coordinator
P.O. Box 1958
Honolulu, HI 96805-1958
Fax: 808-952-7546 or 808-948-8206 (Oahu)

---

**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 5, 2026**

- **Member name:** Quinn Foster
- **Member ID:** W310107367
- **Reference number:** POC-D89C6A76F0-15779
- **Service denied:** Lower back (lumbar) fusion, CPT 22612
- **Plan:** HMSA (Hawaii Medical Service Association), Commercial/ACA, State of Hawaii
- **Governing policy:** *2025 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review – HMSA Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines*, effective July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026 (as printed), available at https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2025-07/2025%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines%20-%20HMSA%20FINAL%20eff%20070125.pdf

---

## Why I am writing

I am appealing the denial of the lumbar fusion (CPT 22612) requested for me by my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated August 5, 2026 states that the request was denied because the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure.

I am asking HMSA to reconsider that decision. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and the records already in my file describe imaging findings that directly match my symptoms and my physical exam. I respectfully ask the reviewer to look at those records again against the plan's own published criteria.

## An important note about the criteria I was given

The criteria identified with my denial, and the excerpts I am able to quote below, come from the **cervical spine** portion of the HMSA Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines. My requested surgery is a **lumbar** fusion. I have not been quoted a lumbar-specific criterion that my request is said to fail, so I cannot match my records line by line to a lumbar standard. I am therefore doing two things in this letter:

1. Showing that the evidence in my chart satisfies the *kind* of requirements the plan's guideline uses — imaging confirmation of nerve root compression that corresponds to the clinical findings, and documented failure of conservative treatment; and
2. Asking HMSA, if the denial is upheld, to identify in writing the exact lumbar criterion and the exact guideline language that my records did not meet, so that I can respond to it.

## The plan's own language, and what my records show

**1. Imaging that corresponds with the clinical findings.** The guideline states:

> "● Imaging studies confirm the presence of spinal cord or spinal nerve root compression (disc herniation or foraminal stenosis) at multiple levels corresponding with the clinical findings."

The imaging in my file does exactly this kind of confirmation. My MRI of the lumbar spine dated May 28, 2026 shows **L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root**. That is documented disc herniation and stenosis producing nerve root compression on imaging.

It also corresponds with my clinical findings. My records document radicular pain into the **right calf** — the same side as the imaged compression — along with positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. The imaging and the examination point to the same nerve, on the same side, at the same level. This is the correspondence between imaging and clinical findings that the guideline asks for.

**2. Failure of conservative treatment.** The guideline requires, alongside radiculopathy from a ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity:

> "● Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;"

And it defines that failure as follows:

> "NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following:"

> "○ Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment;"

> "OR ○ Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment;"

My records meet this comfortably:

- **Supervised physical therapy**, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, for **8 weeks** from **May 14, 2026 to July 9, 2026**, with **24 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. That is a full course, longer than the six-week minimum and well within the last six months.
- **NSAIDs for 8 months** with inadequate relief.
- A **corticosteroid injection on April 11, 2026** that gave only **2 weeks of partial relief**.
- My symptoms have run **12 months of progressive pain in the lower back, unrelieved by rest**, and I still **cannot stand more than 10 minutes**.

The guideline also makes clear what does *not* count as an excuse for incomplete treatment:

> "OR ○ Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute “inability to complete” treatment."

That exclusion does not apply to me. I did not skip or shorten treatment. I completed 24 supervised physical therapy visits over 8 weeks, took NSAIDs for 8 months, and underwent an injection. I did the conservative care, and it did not resolve my condition.

**3. No documented barriers to surgery.** My records note no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## What I am asking for

I am asking HMSA to overturn the denial of CPT 22612 and authorize the lumbar fusion my surgeon has documented that I need. Specifically, I ask that the reviewer:

1. Re-examine the MRI of May 28, 2026 and the corresponding exam findings against the plan's imaging criterion quoted above;
2. Re-examine the physical therapy discharge note, medication history, and injection record against the plan's definition of failed conservative treatment; and
3. If the denial is maintained, state in writing the specific lumbar criterion from the *2025 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review – HMSA Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines* that my records were found not to meet, and identify which document in my file was reviewed in reaching that conclusion.

I am happy to have additional records sent directly from Dr. Okafor's office, and I am willing to speak with the reviewer by phone if that would help.

## Timing and submission

Per the denial notice, my appeal must be received **within 180 days of August 5, 2026, by February 1, 2027**. I am submitting this in writing to HMSA Member Advocacy & Appeals at P.O. Box 1958, Honolulu, HI 96805-1958, or by fax at 808-952-7546 or 808-948-8206 (Oahu), and I am keeping a copy for my records, as submissions are not returned. I understand that requests for external (IRO) review are subject to a **130-day** timeframe, and that the deadlines stated in my denial letter are the authoritative ones. I am following the submission requirements in my Guide to Benefits, and I can be reached by phone at the number above.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. I would appreciate written confirmation that this appeal has been received and a decision within the timeframe my plan allows.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Foster**
Member ID: W310107367
Reference number: POC-D89C6A76F0-15779

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated August 5, 2026
- MRI lumbar spine report dated May 28, 2026
- Physical therapy discharge note (May 14, 2026 – July 9, 2026, 24 visits)
- Office notes from Dr. Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery, dated [date(s) of office notes]
- Injection record dated April 11, 2026
- [Any other records you are enclosing]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
